scenes.heading: Agents get rules. Capacity sets the limit.
bullets: Teams are putting SRE-style controls around agents in production.
Meanwhile open-weight models and inference capacity decide what can actually ship.
scenes.narration: Here is Friday's brief in under two minutes. Agents are getting rules. And capacity is setting the limit.

scenes.heading: Who enforces an agent's limits?

left.title: Another model as judge
lines: A second model reviews each action

right.title: Deterministic guardrail
lines: Limits enforced in code, not by a model
Same input, same decision, every time

scenes.narration: A new open-source guardrail enforces agent limits deterministically, instead of asking another model to judge. The point is predictability. The same action gets the same decision, every time.

scenes.heading: Grafana: hold agents to an SLO
scenes.narration: Grafana proposes measuring agent behaviour the way we already hold services to reliability targets. Give the agent an S L O, and an error budget for how much failure is allowed.

scenes.heading: Citi restricts AI agents from customer accounts
scenes.sub: Citi joins other US banks blocking agents from accounts: access-control friction for agent builders.
scenes.narration: On the other side of the same coin, Citi is the latest US bank to block AI agents from customer accounts. Expect access-control friction.

scenes.heading: Google EnvHarness: fix the environment, not the agent
scenes.narration: Google open-sourced EnvHarness. Instead of changing the agent, it adapts the training environment to the agent's weaknesses.

scenes.heading: Reflection Beam-1.0: big model, small active slice

callout.label: decode latency cut with agent-driven optimization (vLLM, day 0)

scenes.narration: Reflection's Beam is five hundred and one billion parameters in total, but only twenty-three billion are active. vLLM supported it from day zero, and agent-driven optimization cut decode latency two point seven one times.

scenes.heading: Kimi K3 on AMD matches NVIDIA per GPU

items.label: AMD MI355X
items.tag: per-GPU throughput, as reported by vLLM

scenes.narration: vLLM also reports Kimi K3 on AMD's MI355X reaching NVIDIA HGX B300 throughput per GPU. That is a real alternative for serving.

scenes.heading: Capacity is the constraint

nodes.title: Maia
nodes.sub: primary inference system for its own products

scenes.narration: And capacity is the constraint. Reporting links DeepSeek's nearly five hour outage to a chip shortage amid China's AI demand. Microsoft plans to scale Maia to multi-gigawatt inference from twenty twenty-seven, though its efficiency metric is being questioned.
